instructions.content: Check whether a semantic-scholar or google-scholar MCP server is configured and prefer it over the script when available.
NEVER skip the MCP availability check; the script is the fragile fallback and needlessly risks rate-limiting.
Choose the right subcommand: search for keywords, advanced for author and year filters, author for a profile.
Look up an author profile with the author subcommand and --name.
Export a candidate list with --format json --output <path>.
Reuse an existing candidate JSON at /tmp/<topic>-candidates.json rather than re-running the search.
If the paper is already known (arxiv ID, DOI, URL), go straight to triage-paper.
For biomedical literature, use PubMed or a domain-specific source instead of this skill.
NEVER auto-triage search results; always confirm with the user before passing a result to triage-paper.
Present the result list and ask whether the user would like to triage any of the papers.
NEVER loop on blocked responses; on HTTP 429 or a short body, wait 60 seconds and retry once.
If still blocked after the retry, offer the semantic-scholar MCP as a fallback and document the blocker.
NEVER report no results without checking for a silent block; a near-empty body (under about 1 KB) is often a CAPTCHA redirect.
NEVER treat year-range results as exhaustive; qualify them as a sample as returned by Google Scholar.
NEVER treat scraped abstracts as canonical; use results for discovery only and re-fetch from arxiv or the DOI during triage.
On the first run, create a virtual environment and install requirements before running the script.
Return candidates, not conclusions: search is discovery, not triage.
